```{r, include = FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(
  collapse = TRUE, comment = "#>", message = FALSE,
  fig.width = 8, fig.height = 5, out.width = "100%",
  eval = rlang::is_installed("ggplot2")
)
```

mongolmaps provides boundaries, place names and mapping helpers for Mongolia.
The simplified boundaries are included in the package, so the examples
below work without internet access.

Install the packages once:

```{r install, eval = FALSE}
install.packages(c("mongolmaps", "ggplot2"))
```

## Your first map

```{r first-map, fig.alt = "Mongolia showing the boundaries of its aimags and Ulaanbaatar."}
library(mongolmaps)
library(ggplot2)

mn_map(mn_aimags(), title = "Mongolia: aimags and Ulaanbaatar")
```

`mn_aimags()` gets the boundaries. `mn_map()` draws them and returns a
ggplot, which you can change with the usual ggplot2 functions.

## Choose the right boundaries

Mongolia has 21 aimags (provinces) and the capital, Ulaanbaatar. Aimags
contain soums, which contain bags. Ulaanbaatar contains districts
(duureg), which contain khoroos.

| What you need | Function | Included? |
|---|---|---|
| Country outline | `mn_country()` | Yes |
| Four economic regions and Ulaanbaatar | `mn_regions()` | Yes |
| 21 aimags and Ulaanbaatar | `mn_aimags()` | Yes |
| 330 soums and 9 city districts | `mn_soums()` | Yes |
| Ulaanbaatar outline | `mn_ub()` | Yes |
| Nine city districts | `mn_ub_districts()` | Yes |
| 204 khoroos | `mn_khoroos()` | Yes, unofficial boundaries |
| Rural bags | `mn_bags()` | Names and codes; supply your own boundaries |

These functions return an `sf` object: a table with a `geometry` column
that stores the shapes. Useful columns include `pcode` (a unique place
code), `name`, `nso_code`, `parent_pcode` and `area_km2`.

```{r columns}
aimags <- mn_aimags()
knitr::kable(head(sf::st_drop_geometry(aimags)[c("name", "pcode", "nso_code")]))
```

Use `name_en`, `name_mn` or `name_mns` for English, Cyrillic Mongolian or
Latin Mongolian names. [Names and codes](names-and-codes.html) explains
the codes and spelling variants.

## Show part of the country

Select places with `aimag` or `region`. Common spelling variants work too.

```{r map-soums, fig.alt = "Soum boundaries in Khovd, Uvs and Bayan-Ulgii in western Mongolia."}
west <- mn_soums(aimag = c("Khovd", "Uvs", "Bayan-Ulgii"))
mn_map(west, title = "Soums in western Mongolia")
```

Use `mn_aimags(region = "Western")` for the whole western region.
Labels are easier to read when you show one aimag at a time.

## Add towns, rivers and neighbouring countries

These small background layers are included in the package.

```{r map-context, fig.alt = "Mongolia's economic regions with major water features, neighbours and aimag centres."}
mn_map(mn_regions(), fill = name, context = TRUE) +
  geom_sf(
    data = mn_settlements(type = c("capital", "aimag_centre")),
    colour = "firebrick", size = 1
  ) +
  labs(title = "Economic regions and aimag centres", fill = "Region",
       caption = paste(strwrap(mn_citation(c("admin", "naturalearth", "settlements")), width = 95), collapse = "\n"))
```

## Use Mongolian labels

```{r mongolian, fig.alt = "Aimags labelled in Cyrillic Mongolian."}
mn_map(mn_aimags(), label = TRUE, lang = "mn", label_size = 2.5)
```

Set `options(mongolmaps.lang = "mn")` to use Mongolian names by default.
If Cyrillic letters appear as boxes, choose a font that supports them,
for example `+ theme_mn(base_family = "Arial")`.

## Coordinates and detail

Boundaries use longitude and latitude (EPSG:4326). `mn_map()` chooses a
suitable projection for display. Use `mn_aimags(crs = "albers")` for
national equal-area coordinates or `mn_ub(crs = "utm")` for Ulaanbaatar
in UTM zone 48N.

The included shapes are simplified for fast plotting. This optional
command downloads full-resolution boundaries once and saves them for
later use. It needs internet access the first time.

```{r high, eval = FALSE}
khovd <- mn_soums(aimag = "Khovd", resolution = "high")
```

`mn_sources()` lists providers and licences. Use `mn_citation()` for
credit text. Khoroo boundaries and the district lines derived from them
are unofficial; a source snapshot does not establish their effective date.
